ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L561-1 et seq., L561-10 and L561-46 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier); Decree No. 2020-115 of 12 February 2020 on the beneficial-owners register; French Commercial Code (Code de commerce) Articles R123-1, R123-5, R123-166 and R123-222; Law No. 2016-731 of 3 June 2016 on the fight against tax fraud and the reinforcement of AML/CFT obligations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each shareholder, beneficial owner, manager and signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority or notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the 1961 Convention; otherwise consular legalization by the French Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement) for every beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or bank, together with notarization by a licensed notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and corporate extract for any corporate shareholder or intermediate entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn beneficial-ownership declaration and statement of lawful source of funds under Article L561-46 CMF
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each beneficial owner executing before a French notary or competent foreign authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization if executed abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and original proof of foreign funding/source of funds for incoming capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank or financial institution in the remitting jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization where demanded by the receiving French bank

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs and authorized representatives against the French national sanctions list maintained by the Direction générale du Trésor, the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, the United Nations consolidated sanctions list, and, where payment rails or fintech intermediaries are US-linked, the OFAC SDN list. Politically exposed persons and their families/close associates are identified on a risk basis in accordance with FATF standards and Article L561-10 CMF, triggering enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval and source-of-funds verification before incorporation proceeds.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) and INPI Data Inpi (data.inpi.fr) for corporate-name/trademark conflicts
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The draft social name must be submitted in Latin characters; if a non-Latin alphabet is used, an official transliteration and a certified French translation must be attached to the articles of association. The name must lawfully carry the suffix 'SARL' and must not mislead the public as to the actual corporate object. All RCS filings are in French, and the name must not create confusing similarity with an existing RCS entry or an INPI-registered trademark.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms implying state authority: 'Ministère', 'Préfecture', 'Mairie', 'Trésor public', 'République' unless expressly franchised
Terms protected by law or requiring special authorization: 'Banque', 'Caisse d'épargne', 'Assurance', 'Mutuelle', 'Notaire', 'Avocat', 'Commissaire'
Names of recognized international organizations: 'Croix-Rouge', 'Nations Unies', 'UNESCO', 'Commission européenne'
Misleading geographical terms ('Paris', 'France', 'Bordeaux') when the registered office is not situated in that locality
Any term contrary to morality, public order or public decency prohibited under Article 1832 et seq. of the Civil Code
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not provide a separate automatic extension of the pre-lodging name-availability window; a fresh submission may be made through the Guichet unique before expiry of, or immediately after, the initial 30-day window. If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may file a supplementary response via the Guichet unique, resubmitting the same name with additional distinguishing elements; in the case of an INPI trademark objection, an opposition may be lodged with INPI within two months; if the registry (greffe) refuses registration on conflict grounds, a motion to compel registration may be filed with the President of the competent Tribunal judiciaire (formerly Tribunal de grande instance) under ordinary administrative-remedy rules.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Domiciliation at an approved commercial address is acceptable for the SARL registered office only, under Article L123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code. For the ISIC 5610 ghost-kitchen activity, a virtual office cannot serve as the declared operating kitchen; a physical delivery-only kitchen must be registered with the competent veterinary/health authority (DD(ETS)PP/DDPP) and must satisfy hygiene-licence and fire-safety requirements. Therefore, virtual-office facilities are conditionally permissible for the administrative seat only, provided the actual culinary facilities are separately leased and approved.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — approximately 75% probability of at least one unannounced on-site inspection by the Direction départementale de la protection des populations (DDPP) or the Direction générale de la concurrence, de la consommation et de la répression des fraudes (DGCCRF) within the first 12 months of commencing food production, due to food-safety classification under EU/ French hygiene law (Regulation (EC) 852/2004 and CinP).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; fixed engagement commonly EUR 1,500–2,500, hourly rates EUR 200–400

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company-name availability search on INPI Trade Mark / RCS database and legal clearance opinion

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation notice in an authorized legal gazette (annonce légale)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Agreed legal announcement journal (JAL) in the department of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff; approximately EUR 189–210 incl. VAT

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Guichet unique electronic filing, RCS registration and formalities fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / Infogreffe
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed court-registry fee per ministerial decree, commonly EUR 40–80

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Approved virtual-office/domiciliation agreement for the registered office, 12 months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market tariff; typical annual charge EUR 300–600

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Business bank account KYC/PEP compliance handling and account-opening arrangement for the SARL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French licensed credit institution (bank compliance/KYC fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market/conventional bank schedule; frequently EUR 0–450 depending on bank

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Prefecture / health-authority registration of the ghost-kitchen as food business establishment (code NAF 5610A/ISIC 5610)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Direction départementale de la protection des populations (DDPP) / prefecture
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Declaration is free of statutory fee; amount reflects administrative compliance and translation/certification burden

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Articles L.223-1 to L.223-44 (SARL formation, share capital, management and governance); Article L.210-2 (freedom of incorporation formalities); Decree No. 2023-486 on dematerialized company formalities and the Single Formalities Statement (Guichet unique).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) operating the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); electronic filing via the official Guichet unique formalities portal operated by the INPI.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation application combining the CERFA form M0 (déclaration de constitution), the Articles of Association (Statuts), appointment documents, and the legal publication certificate; registration results in the extract Kbis.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an SARL (may be fixed as low as EUR 1); however, the entire share capital must be fully subscribed and each cash contribution must be deposited in a blocked bank account opened in the company's name, released only upon issuance of the RCS registration extract. In-kind contributions above EUR 30,000 or exceeding 50% of the share capital require a statutory capital auditor (commissaire aux apports); cash contributions of any amount exceeding EUR 1,000 require the blocked-account attestation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] SARL. The founders, acting as the assembled shareholders, unanimously resolve: (1) the draft Articles of Association are approved and the company is constituted as a Société à Responsabilité Limitée under the French Commercial Code; (2) the registered office is fixed at [ADDRESS] and the manager may transfer it within the same department upon shareholder ratification; (3) all shares are validly subscribed and cash contributions of EUR [AMOUNT] remain deposited in the blocked account until registration; (4) [NAME] is appointed sole general manager (gérant) with all powers conferred by law and the Articles; (5) the gérant is authorized to execute the official filing, publish the mandatory legal notice, and complete every registration, license, and permit application required for operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Valuation, and Execution of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders; notarial execution optional unless a future transfer of real estate or in-kind contributions requires a notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts in French, stating corporate name, legal form, registered office, share capital, duration (maximum 99 years), corporate purpose (ghost kitchen multi-brand delivery-only catering), appointment of the gérant, and share distribution. Verify the proposed corporate name against the INPI trademark register and RCS availability. Have each shareholder date and sign every copy of the Statuts; certify signatures as required by bank and registry practice.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Association (Statuts)
Identity documents (passport/national ID) of all shareholders
Extract of judicial record (casier judiciaire) or declaration of non-conviction of the gérant
Proof of physical address for the registered office (lease, ownership deed, reçu of domiciliation agreement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or bank queries the Statuts, amend by unanimous quorum resolution and re-sign a consolidated version before submission; any retroactive correction is documented by a rectifying resolution and refiled with the Greffe.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Deposit Account and Payment of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank authorized in France or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the deposit is held for the company in formation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open an account in the name of the company under formation. Each shareholder transfers the full amount of his cash contribution with a precise remittance reference. The bank issues an attestation de blocage des fonds confirming the total amount deposited and the list of subscribers. Funds remain inaccessible until the RCS registration extract is issued, after which the bank releases the capital to the company account.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association or notarized copy
Identity documents of each contributing shareholder
Bank remittance slips / wire confirmations
Completed bank onboarding documents (KYB/KYC questionnaires)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays or rejects the deposit (e.g., beneficial ownership doubts), provide a clear organizational chart and SOF initiation, or alternatively deposit the funds with the Caisse des Dépôts; the attestation is reissued and the timeline restarts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Statutory Legal Notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A legal announcement newspaper (Journal d'Annonces Légales) authorized in the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the legal notice (avis de constitution) containing the corporate name, legal form, capital amount, registered office address, corporate purpose, duration, and the names of the gérant. Submit the notice to the JAL and obtain a certificate of publication (certificat de parution) with the newspaper's attestation; the notice must appear before or simultaneously with the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Legal notice draft (avis de constitution)
Copy of the signed Articles of Association
Bank attestation of blocked capital deposit
Order form and payment to the JAL
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice contains an error, the JAL publishes a corrective notice (rectificatif) in the same newspaper, and the corrected certificate is reissued for the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Incorporation Dossier with the Guichet Unique and Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises operated by the INPI, transmitting the dossier to the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for RCS registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the official CERFA M0/M1 electronic application on the formalities portal. Upload the signed Statuts, legal publication certificate, blocked-account attestation, identity documents, non-conviction declarations for the manager, and declaration of beneficial owner (Déclarant/BO). Select ISIC/NAF code 5610A for restaurant-type delivery activity if the classification is applicable. Pay the registry fee by bank card or transfer. The Greffe verifies legal compliance and issues the extract Kbis and the INSEE SIREN/SIRET number.
required_dossiers: CERFA n°14276*03 incorporation form (electronic)
Signed Articles of Association in .PDF
Certificate of legal publication from the JAL
Bank attestation of blocked capital deposit
Identity document of the gérant
Declaration of non-conviction for the gérant
Completed beneficial owner declaration
Proof of registered office address (lease or domiciliation deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a query or observation (demande de pièces complémentaires), respond within 20 days with corrective documents; the dossier is reassessed and registration is completed once all statutory irregularities are cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of the Registration Certificate (Extrait Kbis) and Statistical Identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and INSEE (National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval of the filing, the Greffe issues an official extrait Kbis certifying legal existence, and INSEE assigns the SIREN, SIRET, and the NAF/APE code. Verify the Kbis entries against the Articles (corporate name, address, gérant, capital, purpose). The legal entity is then authorized to open the definitive company bank account, sign contracts, and apply for operating licenses.
required_dossiers: No additional dossier is required; the Kbis is generated electronically from the validated registration file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis contains an error in purpose, designation, or capital, request an immediate rectification from the Greffe via the formalities portal; the correction is processed within 5 days and a clean Kbis is reissued.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction départementale de l'emploi, du travail, des solidarités et de la protection des populations (DDETSPP) for food business opening declaration; the environmental police of the competent Préfecture (Inspection des Installations Classifiées) for industrial regime determination.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Déclaration d'ouverture d'un établissement de restauration (food business registration) under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and the French rural and maritime fishing code, together with an ICPE exploitation registration for catering facilities falling under the Code de l'environnement, and a municipal business establishment license (permis d'exploitation).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique et de la Cohésion des Territoires — Inspection des Installations Classifiées pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: simplified environmental assessment (examen au cas par cas / notice d'incidence) — ghost kitchens normally fall under the ICPE 'déclaration' (registration) regime; a full EIA report is not required unless the facility's cooking capacity, cold-storage ammonia volume, or effluents exceed the threshold in Article R.214-1 of the Environmental Code or generate a major industrial risk as defined in the ICPE nomenclature.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge conforming to municipal sewer standards (grease traps and pre-treatment units); compliance with the Arrêté of 2 February 1998 for VOCs and odorous fumes emitted by kitchen ventilation hoods; refrigeration installations must respect the F-gas Regulation (EU) No 517/2014 for fluorinated greenhouse gases; food waste and cooking oil must be tracked by a licensed waste collector with delivery notices; nighttime noise and odor abatement obligations per the specific arrêté préfectoral.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification delivered by the fire and rescue service (SDIS) and the commission de sécurité; the operational building licence includes a structural load proof certified by a qualified inspection office, verification of electrical installations per NF C 15-100, emergency lighting and extraction systems; occupational clearance requires the workplace medical service (médecine du travail), the single occupational risk assessment document (DUERP), and compliance with Labor Code provisions for ventilation, equipment guarding, and hygiene of food handling areas.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP); central taxpayer portal 'impots.gouv.fr'; business filings and registrations through the Guichet Unique (INPI) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; corporate tax returns filed via 'Espace Professionnel' / e-services GEDI.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A newly formed SARL obtains its legal identity and tax identification through the Guichet Unique operated by INPI. After RCS (Registre du commerce et des sociétés) registration, DGFIP automatically assigns a SIREN (9-digit national company identifier), a SIRET workplace identifier, and a French intra-Community VAT number (format FR[two-digit key] + SIREN) for VAT-registered activities. A foreign non-EU company engaged directly in French taxable activities must apply proactively to the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) of its place of business or to the non-resident tax office (Service des impôts des particuliers / non-résidents) using Form 1447? or the dedicated Article 289 B registration procedure, submitting constitutional documents, proof of permanent establishment/economic activity in France, and confirmation of the appointed French tax representative/representative fiscal if no permanent establishment. The application must be made before the first taxable supply in France.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election under French law. A standard commercial SARL is by default subject to French corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). The CGI provides a limited transparency election for eligible 'SARL de famille' under Article 239 bis AA CGI, allowing taxation at the level of individual partners in place of entity-level IS when the statutory family-shareholding conditions are met. Contrariwise, an EURL (SARL with a single natural-person member) is treated as a transparent societé de personnes unless it opts irreversibly into IS under Article 206.4 CGI. For cross-border scenarios, France applies the ATAD anti-hybrid rules (Articles 212 bis, 212 ter CGI) which deny deductions or recharacterize payments where another jurisdiction treats an SARL as transparent or applies a different entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA / French Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: General domestic goods-supply threshold under the franchise en base de TVA (CGI art. 293 B): EUR 85,000 of annual taxable turnover, with a tolerance upper threshold of EUR 93,500; for services the base threshold is EUR 37,500 with upper tolerance EUR 41,000. A ghost kitchen delivery business whose principal supply consists of prepared meals generally counts as a supply of goods for VAT registration purposes, but the threshold must be assessed per legal unit and includes all taxable turnover, including supplies made through delivery platforms; marketplaces may also trigger separate VAT obligations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is progressively mandating structured electronic invoicing and e-reporting through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) and certified private dematerialisation platforms (PDPs). Large taxpayers must issue e-invoices and report B2B/B2C transaction data to the FTA from 1 September 2026; SMEs and micro-enterprises are phased in from 1 September 2027. The system is not an ex-ante fiscal clearing model like Italy's SdI but requires near-real-time e-reporting of B2C transactions, digital stamping/completion of the invoice data via interoperability API, and retention of an authenticated audit trail. Invoicing software must also satisfy the French anti-fraud certification requirement (CGI art. 286 III, BOI-TVA-DECL-30-30-20 and 30-40-20).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, VAT zero-rating applies where the SARL proves that the goods were physically exported from France to a destination outside the European Union within the prescribed statutory period, ownership risk has passed to the EU/non-EU purchaser, and the goods have left the French customs territory, in compliance with CGI Article 262-I. For offshore services, zero-rating depends on place-of-supply rules: services physically performed or effectively used outside the EU, services related to immovable property situated outside the EU, and certain intangibles supplied to a business customer established outside the EU are generally outside French VAT. The seller must hold documentary evidence showing the actual export and reception of payment; self-billed zero-rated invoices must mention the legal basis for the 0% rate. A French ghost kitchen operator exporting prepared-food products or franchise/IP services must evidence the cross-border movement and the commercial substance of the export transaction to avoid reclassification as domestic VATable supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration filed via the DELTA/GUN system (DAU / ECS Summary Declaration) proving exit of the goods
Transport document evidencing physical movement: Bill of Lading (sea), Air Waybill, CMR road consignment note, or rail consignment note
Commercial invoice and export packing list
Proof of receipt/payment from the foreign customer, including Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer confirmation evidencing currency repatriation to France
Export order contract / incoterms evidence and any certificate of origin where required
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFIP may audit every VAT zero-rating claim. If the documentary file is incomplete or a transaction is deemed to be a domestic supply or an intra-EU supply, the taxpayer is immediately liable for output VAT at the applicable rate (currently 5.5%, 10% or 20% depending on the product), plus late-payment interest (intérêt de retard). Underscore: fraudulent zero-rating attracts the 80% penalty for bad-faith or abusive tax evasion (CGI art. 1729), an additional 40% penalty if the misstatement is intentional, possible administrative fines under HNOA, and criminal prosecution for fraud (fraude fiscale) with penalties up to EUR 500,000/EUR 1,000,000 and custodial sentences. Retrospective clawback is unlimited for concealed or fictitious exports, and the taxpayer bears the burden of substantiating the export.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) — monetary authority and responsible for balance-of-payments statistics; exchange-control and foreign-investment policy is coordinated with the Direction Générale du Trésor; banking and e-money licensing and supervision are delegated to the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France grants full currency convertibility for both current-account and capital-account transactions, in accordance with Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the EU free movement of capital regime. The euro is fully convertible; there are no surrender or repatriation impediments. Profit remittances by a French SARL to non-resident shareholders are permitted without exchange-control authorisation, subject to corporate law conditions: existence of distributable profit, compliance with legal reserve requirements, and shareholder approval. The practical hurdles are documentary and statistical, not regulatory: the cross-border transfer must be reported to the Banque de France via the intermediary credit institution, using the appropriate balance-of-payments purpose code and including tax-residence documentation of the beneficial owner. Withholding-tax exposure on dividends or interest is separate from FX-control and must be assessed under domestic and treaty rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender regime. There is no mandatory conversion ratio and no fixed deadline for repatriating export receipts. Export proceeds may be held in foreign currency, converted at the corporate's discretion, or used directly to settle foreign-currency import obligations. However, cross-border transactions involving French resident entities must be declared for balance-of-payments statistical purposes if the amount exceeds the applicable regulatory threshold (typically EUR 10,000 or the per-transaction reporting threshold), through the authorised intermediary bank. The underlying export contracts, customs declarations (DEB), and commercial invoices must be maintained to substantiate the purpose and lawful origin of the funds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank / LCL

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for the operational treasury and low for the statutory capital escrow function. French-regulated electronic money institutions (e.g., Qonto, Shine, and licensed neobanks) are viable for daily euro and multi-currency accounts, receiving platform payouts from Uber Eats and DoorDash, and executing inbound and outbound SEPA payments. These EMIs operate under the ACPR e-money licence or as registered payment institutions under PSD2, and they are permitted to provide payment accounts and payment services but are not full credit institutions; they cannot offer the official attestation de dépôt des fonds required for the establishment of a SARL capital. Offshore EMIs that lack an EU or ACPR-recognised licence cannot lawfully provide payment services to a French SARL under the mandatory EU passporting or equivalence requirements; using an unlicensed offshore EMI would expose the company to banking-license, AML/CFT, and wire-transfer-decision enforcement risk. Therefore, the capital contribution must be held in a Tier-1 commercial bank, while the foreign-expansion payout accounts may be opened at an ACPR-regulated EMI for operational efficiency.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a French SARL with non-resident shareholders or a complex ownership chain, French credit institutions generally require the statutory manager (gérant) to attend an in-branch interview for the initial high-risk account onboarding. Remote or video-identification onboarding is accepted only where the bank has implemented an eIDAS-compliant electronic identification solution and has assessed the corporate customer as lower risk. Since a ghost-kitchen operation may have no physical bank-visible storefront, the bank will almost certainly impose physical attendance of the legal representative and the supply-chain documents before activating the account. A full KYC interview should be scheduled at the managing branch; after the initial physical verification, digital signing and remote transactions become routine.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity where foreign shareholders hold the SARL through an offshore holding vehicle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a certified corporate chart listing all natural-person ultimate beneficial owners; a notarised copy of the SARL share register (registre des mouvements de titres); a KBis extract; passport copies and proof of tax residence; and a written explanation of the commercial purpose for the foreign holding structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-identifiable commercial substance of a delivery-only ghost kitchen with a virtual brand and no physical restaurant frontage
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the commercial lease for the production kitchen; the SIREN/SIRET registration of the operating site; the hygiene registration certificate (agrément sanitaire) issued by the Direction Départementale de la Protection des Populations; a food-business-operations plan; the active contracts with Uber Eats or DoorDash; and trademark or intellectual-property proof for the virtual brand.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High expected transaction velocity and cash-equivalent payout settlement from multiple delivery platforms
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a month-one cash-flow forecast; a copy of the settlement schedule and payout reporting templates used by the delivery platforms; a signed declaration of the payment-flow architecture that clearly distinguishes gross settlement, commission, VAT, and operating disbursements; and a written commitment to maintain a platform-reconciliation audit trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicion that the bank account may be used for money transmission in place of authorised payment services
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a copy of the underlying service-level agreements with the delivery platforms demonstrating that the platforms are the merchants of record for each order; confirm that the SARL operates as the food-preparation service provider only; produce pro-forma invoices and business contracts showing that the account receives remuneration for meal production, not for third-party funds transfer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from a non-resident shareholder to the French SARL must be executed via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 COV for interbank pass-through) from the shareholder's bank, with the remittance information field explicitly stating 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION / DÉPÔT DU CAPITAL SOCIAL' and referencing the SARL's corporate name and the statutory manager. The receiving French bank will file the cross-border transaction declaration with the Banque de France using the harmonised purpose code for direct investment or capital injection (e.g., code 900/EDP in Banque de France nomenclature) and will verify that the funds originate from a permissible source under AML/CFT. Before the SARL registration, the funds must be deposited in a blocked capital-escrow account with a French credit institution or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations or a notary; the bank issues a 'certificat de dépôt des fonds' that is submitted to the RCS to complete incorporation. After registration, the funds are released to the operational account. The transfer must be supported by a shareholder resolution approving the capital injection, proof of shareholder identity, and a long-term lending agreement if the injection is shareholder debt rather than equity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade and procurement settlements, the SARL may use the SWIFT MT103 for direct euro or foreign-currency payments, which is the most common rail for paying ingredient suppliers and equipment vendors. SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) is the efficient rail for euro-denominated payments to EU counterparties, while SWIFT MT103 remains necessary for non-EEA wires. For high-value procurement, a commercial irrevocable documentary letter of credit can be established by the French bank under the ICC UCP600 and settled through SWIFT MT754 and MT799 reimbursement messages. Cash-in-advance and open-account settlement are supported by the same MT103 infrastructure. The remittance instructions must include the invoice number, a transparent purpose description, and, where relevant, the customs tariff classification so that the bank can complete the required external-debt or balance-of-payments reporting for Banque de France.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Foreign-exchange outright forwards (vente à terme) governed by the French master agreement for forward foreign-exchange and interbank operations
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps under ISDA 2002 and local French Banking Federation (FBF) master agreements for long-term exposure management
FX options, including vanilla put-and-call options, permitted when backed by an underlying commercial transaction
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with limited convertibility or sub-Saharan and Asian jurisdictions where local delivery is statutorily restricted
Currency swap structures with notional exchange and reverse exchange at maturity, provided the exposure is documented as hedging a contracted import or export flow

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory financial statements (balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, annexes and management report where applicable) approved by the shareholders and deposited with the commercial court registry (dépôt des comptes annuels au greffe), including the optional Article L.232-25 confidentiality declaration to restrict public disclosure of the accounts.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS court registry) and Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) operated by INPI via the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual: ordinary shareholders' meeting within six months of fiscal year-end (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end); registry deposit within one month of approval (standard deadline 31 July for calendar-year companies); single-member SARL: decision recorded in the decision register within the same six-month statutory limit.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing triggers a criminal fine up to EUR 2,000 per natural-person manager and EUR 10,000 per legal entity (Code de commerce Art. L.232-23); the Commercial Court may appoint a court-mandated agent to convene the meeting at the manager's expense; two consecutive unfiled fiscal years expose the SARL to judicial or administrative radiation (strike-off) from the RCS with loss of legal standing until fresh accounts are filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Minutes of the Ordinary Annual General Meeting (procès-verbal d'assemblée générale ordinaire) approving the annual accounts, deciding the allocation of profits, and ratifying or reviewing the actions of the gérant; record of the annual report where statutorily required.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Statutory decision register and minute book (registre des décisions des associés and registre des procès-verbaux) maintained at the registered office; no separate filing authority, but the minutes serve as the legal basis for the annual accounts deposit and any dividend distribution.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of each fiscal year-end (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end); courts may grant an extension only on justified application.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the annual meeting within the six-month limit is punishable by criminal fine up to EUR 2,000 per natural-person manager and EUR 10,000 per legal entity (Code de commerce Art. L.241-5 for SARL); any shareholder may petition the Commercial Court to order convocation at the gérant's personal expense; accounts cannot be validly deposited and dividend payments remain blocked until the meeting takes place.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Updated declaration of beneficial owner(s) (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) filed with the registry, accompanied by certified transfer deeds and entries in the share movement register (registre des mouvements de titres) covering any cession de parts, pledge of shares, or change in the ownership chain during the fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) operated by INPI through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises; underlying UBO dossier held at the registered office for inspection by supervisory authorities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days following any direct or indirect change in shareholding, voting rights or control (including transfers between associates); registry data must be re-validated at each annual accounts filing and at each 31 December cycle; SARL share transfers must first be inscribed in the share movement register to become opposable to the company and to third parties.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines under the Monetary and Financial Code up to EUR 7,500 per natural person and EUR 37,500 per legal entity (quintupling rule), with up to six months' imprisonment for deliberate concealment or false UBO statements; un-inscribed transfers remain unopposable to the SARL and third-party claimants; persistent non-declaration exposes the company to administrative strike-off and blockage of dividend distributions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business rates declaration and payment (cotisation foncière des entreprises, CFE) covering the ghost-kitchen operating premises; the filing evidences the taxable premises, rental or ownership basis, and the utility contracts supporting kitchen activity.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) through the professional online account and the local Service des Impôts des Entreprises of the operating commune.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual: principal payment and declaration due by mid-December for the current liability year (soft deadline 15 December); new businesses generally benefit from a two-year exemption after creation and must declare new premises by 31 December of the year of start-up; an advance instalment of 50% is payable in June and the balance in December where annual CFE exceeds EUR 3,000.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment or return triggers a 10% penalty plus 0.20% monthly interest (intérêts de retard) applied by DGFiP with enforced recovery by tax lien; sustained non-payment can interrupt payment gateway settlements and platform payouts, a material cash-flow risk for delivery-only virtual-brand operations; a minimum CFE of approximately EUR 229 applies even where the kitchen reports zero turnover for the year.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Appointment of an independent statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory under Code de commerce Art. L.223-3-1 and D.223-2 when, at the closing date, at least two of three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive fiscal years: (i) balance sheet total above EUR 4,000,000; (ii) net turnover excluding VAT above EUR 8,000,000; (iii) average permanent workforce above 50 employees. The thresholds were reduced from EUR 6,000,000 / EUR 12,000,000 for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2024. A court may also appoint an auditor on the application of a shareholder, and the audit is mandatory for certain consolidated groups irrespective of these thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory accounts must be prepared under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, Règlement ANC n°2014-03, as amended), expressed in euros and French language; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted only for consolidated financial statements of listed or certain large groups; ghost-kitchen revenue from delivery platforms must be recorded in turnover accounts reflecting the platform voucher settlement and agency-versus-principal recognition per the applicable French accounting interpretations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Article L.561-46 of the Monetary and Financial Code requires identification of each beneficial owner (direct or indirect control, 25% capital or voting rights threshold) and declaration to the registry. Any transfer of SARL shares triggers mandatory updating of the UBO file and deposit with the Greffe within 30 days through the Guichet Unique. France does not impose a standalone annual UBO declaration; instead, entities must re-affirm and correct the registry UBO data at every annual accounts deposit, conduct an annual review as at 31 December, and maintain a complete UBO dossier at the registered office containing identification documents and the control chain, available for inspection by AML authorities and French credit institutions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Shareholders (registre des associés de la SARL) and Share Movement Register (registre des mouvements de titres)
Register of Manager Resolutions and General Meeting Decisions (registre des décisions de la gérance et des assemblées)
Minute Book (registre des procès-verbaux d'assemblées générales) with attendance sheets and powers of attorney
UBO register file (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) containing evidence of the ownership and control chain

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$650–$2,200 (EUR 600–EUR 2,000) per year for a fully compliant commercial domiciliation service (registered office, mail handling and regulatory correspondence), with Paris pricing at the upper end of the range under PACTE Act domiciliation rules; a standard corporate secretarial retainer for minute book maintenance and registry filings ranges from US$1,100 to US$3,300 (EUR 1,000–EUR 3,000).
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$4,500–$16,000 (EUR 4,000–EUR 15,000) for a first-year statutory certification mission by a commissaire aux comptes for a mid-size SARL; EUR 3,000–EUR 6,000 (approx. US$3,300–$6,600) for the recurring annual audit of a small single-entity SARL below consolidation requirements; joint auditors are not required for an ordinary SARL unless the entity heads a consolidated group.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SME reduced rate of 15% on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for companies meeting applicable conditions (CGI art. 219). A 3.3% social contribution applies to corporate income tax where turnover exceeds EUR 7.63 million. Possible territorial exemptions for new enterprises in priority development zones and the JEI regime for innovative companies apply only if the entity meets the statutory criteria.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory expiry; annual deduction capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable income exceeding that threshold, with carryback limited to one year under exceptional statutory windows)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: French corporate income tax return form no. 2065-SD (Cerfa) filed electronically via EDI-TDFC on the impots.gouv.fr professional portal; annexes 2051 to 2058-SD as applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the return must be filed by the second working day after 1 May. For other fiscal year-ends, the filing deadline is the date set by the posting of the provisional schedule, normally within three months of the financial year-end. An additional 15% first-instalment payment obligation applies for companies whose prior year tax exceeded EUR 3,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cross-border SARL identity: SIREN, RCS registration, address of the place of management, legal form, and activity code (5610).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL itself is the taxpayer; non-resident shareholders do not file this return. The SARL must include the identity and residence of non-resident directors and shareholders in the attached form no. 2059-F-SD when such information is requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit determined after statutory adjustments (e.g. non-deductible expenses, depreciation, provisions, Franco-fiscal reclassification). This is the basis for the 15% reduced rate band and the 25% standard rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL accounts must be prepared by a certified public accountant (expert-comptable); non-resident shareholders must ensure all inter-company charges are arm's-length and documented before this figure is entered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax loss for the fiscal year eligible for carryforward under the current-year cap of EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the excess taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No special non-resident action required; the SARL may claim the carryforward against future profits, subject to the statutory annual utilisation cap.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line AF – Plus-values et pertes en capital
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net short- and long-term capital gains and losses from disposals of fixed assets, including goodwill, kitchen equipment, and delivery-platform contracts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners should verify that any asset sale between the SARL and its foreign parent is priced at fair market value and that the corresponding transfer-pricing file is maintained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims for available corporate tax credits, including the research tax credit (CIR), innovation tax credit (CII), and any territorial employment credits that may apply to delivery-operations headcount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits are claimed by the SARL only. A non-resident parent cannot directly offset these credits against French dividend withholding tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted filing triggers a 10% late-filing penalty on the assessed corporate income tax, escalated to 40% if a formal notice remains unfilled and 80% for intentional concealment. Interest for late payment runs at 0.2% per month. Additionally, a fixed penalty of EUR 20 applies for each omitted supporting document.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under CGI art. 119 bis for dividends distributed by a French SARL to a non-resident company or non-resident individual account unless a specific statutory exemption applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a 0% rate under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (5% minimum capital holding, 24-month holding period) or a lower treaty rate, the non-resident parent must provide to the French paying agent a certificate of tax residence (attestation de résidence fiscale) and, where relevant, an ownership attestation evidencing the holding period. For treaty cases, form no. 5000 (cerfa) may be used to request a reduced withholding at source; if not obtainable before payment, the parent can claim a refund within the French statutory prescription period (until 31 December of the third year following the distribution).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate under CGI art. 119 bis: 25% on royalties and 25% on interest paid to non-residents. Under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive, 0% applies between associated companies of different EU Member States meeting the same ownership and holding conditions; most French DTAs reduce interest to 0%–10% and royalties to 0%–15%, subject to full beneficial ownership and substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 – a French SARL is subject to mandatory transfer pricing documentation (local file, master file) if its annual turnover or total balance-sheet assets exceed EUR 50 million or it belongs to a group whose French subsidiary meets these thresholds. Below that threshold, the documentation must still be prepared and provided upon the tax administration's specific request if material cross-border transactions exist, based on the level of controlled international transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) filing register. The substance of a French SARL is established through GAAR article L64 of the LPF and the anti-abuse rule under CGI art. 205 A. A ghost-kitchen SARL must evidence real physical kitchen premises, employed delivery-coordination staff, platform contracts with actual external meal-service operators, and bookkeeping that supports the arm's-length nature of all fees paid or received. Without such substance the tax administration may disregard artificial arrangements and recharacterise transactions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting UberEats/DoorDash payout revenue, registering phantom staff to claim payroll credits, or concealing sales in unlinked foreign bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under CGI art. 1741, fine up to EUR 75,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; aggravation by organized group raises the penalty to EUR 200,000 and 7 years. The tax administration concurrently demands 80% of the evaded tax as a punitive assessment plus late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors as natural persons incur joint and several civil liability for the evaded tax and penalties; in aggravated cases travel bans, freezing of personal bank accounts, and imprisonment are imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Arrangement / Abuse of Law (Abus de droit)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inserting a shell intermediary in a zero-tax state solely to receive royalties on virtual-brand recipes sold to the French kitchen, or entering into a circular financing scheme with no commercial purpose except to avoid French corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under LPF art. L64, the tax administration disregards the artificial act and reassesses tax as if it had not occurred, plus a penalty of 80% if the taxpayer cannot prove good faith; otherwise the penalty is 40%. Monthly late-payment interest accrues at 0.2%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors having signed the underlying fraudulent contracts are personally liable for the increased assessment and any unpaid corporate tax; where the abuse amounts to fraud, criminal liability under art. 1741 attaches with imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SARL to launder criminal proceeds through fictitious delivery invoices, converting hidden cash into unrestricted digital assets, or structuring platform payouts to evade banking anti-money-laundering controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: French Monetary and Financial Code arts. L.574-1 et seq. punish laundering of proceeds of aggravated tax fraud with up to 10 years’ imprisonment and a fine of up to EUR 750,000; the privilege of conducting commercial activities may be suspended and the corporate entity dissolved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who organise or direct the scheme face criminal fines multiplied by the corporate fine framework (up to EUR 1,000,000 for natural persons), permanent prohibition from managing a company, and asset seizure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to establish and produce transfer-pricing documentation for brand royalties, technical service fees, cost allocations, or set-off mechanisms between the French ghost-kitchen operation and the non-resident parent, or deliberately pricing the controlled transactions outside the arm's-length range.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CGI art. 1735-B imposes a fine equal to 5% of the amount of the undocumented transfers, capped at EUR 50,000 per financial year, in addition to a tax reassessment under domestic arm's-length rules and mandatory interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the incomplete documentation results in a mis-assessment, directors may be held personally liable for the unpaid corporate tax under la responsabilité solidaire; fraudulent intent invokes the 5-year/€75,000 criminal penalty of art. 1741 and a potential travel ban during the criminal investigation.
